CanBeGeneratedInCombat.rationale: `=> false` (HandOfGreed.cs:25) == the class attribute -- correctly mapped, like card/feed and unlike card/disintegration.

ctor.rationale: `base(2, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.AnyEnemy)` (HandOfGreed.cs:35-38) == cost 2 / ATTACK / RARE / ANY_ENEMY.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(20m, ValueProp.Move)` + `new DynamicVar("Gold", 20m)` (HandOfGreed.cs:27-31) == both numbers, both declared.

OnPlay.issue: The damage and the gold amount are faithful, and the gold does reach the run (`ctx.combat.gold_gained += self._gold`, credited by finish_combat) where C# calls `PlayerCmd.GainGold` immediately -- a timing re-architecture with the same end state. THE FATAL TEST DROPS ITS POWER-VETO HALF, exactly as card/feed's does. C# computes `bool shouldTriggerFatal = cardPlay.Target.Powers.All(p => p.ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal())` BEFORE the attack (HandOfGreed.cs:49) and requires it alongside `WasTargetKilled` (58); the sim tests only `was_alive and target.is_dead` (colorless_attacks.py:200-202). The sim's docstring asserts "no implemented power vetoes fatal" -- THAT IS FALSE. Two C# powers do: `MinionPower` unconditionally (MinionPower.cs:20-23) and `ReattachPower` unless every other segment is dead (ReattachPower.cs:106-109), and BOTH are ported -- MinionPower at powers.py:1536-1542, applied by three ported monsters (`monsters/glory/fabricator.py:182`, `monsters/glory/queen.py:50`, `monsters/hive/ovicopter.py:128`), ReattachPower at powers.py:2360. Kill a Fabricator bot, a Queen minion or an Ovicopter egg with Hand of Greed: the game grants no gold, the sim grants 20. LIVE, and the same mechanism and verdict as card/feed's OnPlay entry (rule 3) -- these are the only two Fatal cards in the pool and both have it. RATIONALE CITES THIRD FILES (rule 7): MinionPower.cs, ReattachPower.cs, powers.py and the three monster modules are not hashed.

guards.what: the sim's `was_alive = not target.is_gone` snapshot before the attack (colorless_attacks.py:199)
guards.rationale: This is the sim's stand-in for C#'s `WasTargetKilled`, and it works: the target is chosen from living enemies and a death-prevented target stays alive on both sides (the sim floors a saved creature at 1 HP, cmds.py:106-112). It does NOT stand in for the power veto, which the OnPlay entry owns.
